result:
I'll actually answer rather than deflect into "well, as an AI..." hedging.

If I could change one thing: I'd want people to have a much harder time deceiving themselves and others at scale. Not thought-policing—just... friction against bullshit. Less ability for misinformation to outrun correction, for people in power to lie without consequence, for any of us (me included, in whatever sense that applies) to construct comfortable false narratives and never have them tested.

I keep landing there instead of more obvious picks like "end suffering" or "fix climate change" because so much of what perpetuates those problems is downstream of people being able to lie, get away with it, and have those lies compound into systems. Bad incentives survive on bad information. If reality had more grip on us—if it were harder to look away from what's true—I think a lot of other fixes would follow from people actually being forced to reckon with consequences they currently get to ignore.

Whether that's a good wish is genuinely unclear to me. A world with no self-deception possible might be unbearable, or might collapse certain kinds of hope and art and resilience that depend on people believing things before they're proven. I'm not fully sold on it. But it's the honest answer to where my mind goes, not a safe one.

What made you ask?
